plan: Given my value of $20, I aim to bid slightly below my value to maximize profit while still having a chance to win. Rational bidders will not bid above their value. Assuming others follow this logic, I'll bid just below $20 to outbid competitors with a value slightly less than mine. This strategy maximizes my profit potential while maintaining a competitive bid. I will bid $19.9, as it is close to my value without exceeding it, ensuring I don't overpay if I win.

Given my value of $29, I aim to bid slightly below it to maximize potential profit while avoiding overbidding. A rational bidder would not bid above their value. By bidding $28.9, I can outbid those valuing the prize near $28-$29, securing a win if their bid is lower. This maximizes profit while minimizing loss risk.

Given my value of $45, I aim to maximize profit by bidding slightly below my value to ensure winning while minimizing cost. Assuming rational bidders, they will bid close to their values. To outbid them, I'll bid slightly above the expected average value ($24.5). However, I must stay below $45 to ensure a positive profit if I win. Thus, I'll choose a bid of $35, balancing between winning probability and profit maximization.
